seats.oldValue: At the gap in the hedge.
seats.newValue: At the gap in the hedge.
seats.execution: The gap in the hedge is line 22, where the elderly rabbit stops him, well after lines 14 and 15. The child answers from a later part of the passage instead of the lines the stem names, where he is rolling in the meadow grass.

Nothing says the meadow was new to the Mole; line 15 only has him rolling in it. A creature from underground meeting a meadow makes 'never seen before' sound likely, but line 29 says it only of the river.

seats.oldValue: To show the family were well organised.
seats.newValue: To show the family were well organised.
seats.execution: The child reads the content of the numbering, each helper given a job, as if the household were orderly. The question is about the shape: counting a second, a third, a fourth, a fifth piles more people on with every word.

seats.oldValue: He has learned, as he did not know then, that the job was hard.
seats.newValue: He has learned, as he did not know then, that the job was hard.
seats.execution: Line 62 has him survey the mess with evident pride and say some people would have had a man in. The passage states the contrary of a lesson learned; he is as sure of himself at the end as at the start.

seats.oldValue: We get no feelings from him at all, only what his friend Ilya says.
seats.newValue: We get no feelings from him at all, only what his friend Ilya says.
seats.execution: The option keeps the key's shape, nothing from inside Reuben and only one other source, and changes that one detail to Ilya's talk. The child matches on gist and misses that Ilya talks of lockers, Whitby and cupboards and never of Reuben.

seats.oldValue: An argument between two of the rabbits.
seats.newValue: An argument between two of the rabbits.
seats.execution: The child gives the row to the wrong parties. Lines 22 to 25 have the Mole bowl over the elderly rabbit and jeer at the others as they peep from their holes; no two rabbits quarrel with each other.

seats.oldValue: Everybody who came to the assembly that night.
seats.newValue: Everybody who came to the assembly that night.
seats.execution: The child has the right kind of meaning, a group of people, at the wrong size: everyone at the assembly. Lines 21 and 22 count the party that entered as five people who came in together.

seats.oldValue: To make sure the reader counts the guests carefully.
seats.newValue: To make sure the reader counts the guests carefully.
seats.execution: The child supplies a purpose for the writer, making the reader count, that nothing in lines 17 to 23 supports. The three numbers change as the news passes round the village, and nobody is asked to count them.

seats.oldValue: Beauty was too frightened of the water to cross the bridge.
seats.newValue: Beauty was too frightened of the water to cross the bridge.
seats.execution: Lines 36 to 38 have Beauty not dare go forward, and line 41 gives the reason: he knew the bridge was not safe. The child supplies fear of the water itself, a likely reason for a horse to balk, which the passage never gives.

seats.oldValue: To show how long the job took to finish.
seats.newValue: To show how long the job took to finish.
seats.execution: Lines 27 to 29 count helpers who are all standing round at the same moment. The child reads 'a second, a third, a fourth, a fifth' as stages one after another, and so as time passing, when the count piles more people into one scene.

seats.oldValue: He is pleased, and glad they all helped so much at the end.
seats.newValue: He is pleased, and glad they all helped so much at the end.
seats.execution: Uncle Podger is proud at line 62, but his gladness at the family's help is what the passage denies: at line 37 he calls them all fools, and at line 52 he scolds the women for making a fuss. The child gives him gratitude the text states the contrary of.

seats.oldValue: He describes only the old clothes, and so we get nothing else.
seats.newValue: He describes only the old clothes, and so we get nothing else.
seats.execution: The passage describes much more than old clothes: Ilya's talk, Miss Bhatt, the football sheet at lines 37 to 39 and the folded paper at lines 35 and 36. The child claims the telling gives clothes and nothing else, which the passage contradicts, and so misses that Reuben's feeling is carried by what he handles.

seats.oldValue: She thinks the garden will turn out to be a disappointment.
seats.newValue: She thinks the garden will turn out to be a disappointment.
seats.execution: Line 18 has Roberta say they mustn't think of the garden yet, so that the work can start, and she gives no view of the garden at all. The child reads the putting-off as a low opinion of the garden, which the passage never states.

seats.oldValue: Thinking hard about the errands ahead.
seats.newValue: Thinking hard about the errands ahead.
seats.execution: Line 34 gives the errands to be done in Milltown as one of the things that lulled Mr Cobb. The child takes that cause, which is inside the window, for the state it brought on; 'oblivion' names the forgetting itself.

seats.oldValue: Somebody who has paid for a seat.
seats.newValue: Somebody who has paid for a seat.
seats.execution: Paying runs through other parts of the passage: the mother pays the fare at line 16, Rebecca asks whether it costs any more at line 45, and Mr Cobb says there is no extra charge at line 50. The child answers from those lines, where lines 57 and 58 set a real passenger against a hen shut up in a coop.

seats.oldValue: He gives them human names, and leaves the animal ones behind.
seats.newValue: He gives them human names, and leaves the animal ones behind.
seats.execution: The passage calls them the Mole, the Rat and the rabbit on every appearance, so it states the contrary of human names. The child supplies a familiar way of making animals act like people, which this writer does not use.

seats.oldValue: To show that the Mole was creeping closer with every step.
seats.newValue: To show that the Mole was creeping closer with every step.
seats.execution: Nothing in lines 48 to 52 moves the Mole; he is looking, and it is the face that comes into view a piece at a time. The child supplies an approach, a likely thing to go with details arriving one by one, which the passage never states.

seats.oldValue: In a boat painted blue and white.
seats.newValue: In a boat painted blue and white.
seats.execution: The blue and white boat is line 60, near the end of the passage, long after he comes out into the sunlight. The child answers from that later part instead of lines 14 and 15, where he finds himself rolling in a meadow.
The sunlight is line 14, where his snout first comes out of the tunnel. The child answers from that earlier part instead of lines 29 to 33, where the thing he had never seen before is the river.

noEntry.missingMistake: Puts two real events from the passage in reversed order: the child keeps both events and swaps which came first. Neither is a cause placed after its effect, so en-chronology-collapse does not describe it.
